reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The request names the failure "Nothing in the stored event shows the unmet criterion being checked before the final verdict". It asks that the failing stage be given the missing information through "its brief, the system facts it is shown, or the inputs its reader receives". The stored event is the introspection `Event` built in `event_of_job` (introspect.rs:1473-1508), from outcome.reason plus verification failure details only. The reading instead treats it as the producer invocation record, and claims a passing check "leaves no stored event". But the passing report's criteria_check is already stored in `candidate.producer_report`. The real gap is that introspection's input never includes it, and the reading's fix does not touch that input. (round 1 of 5). The plan matches the accepted reading: it makes the producer's per-criterion self-check get written to the producer's invocation `detail` on every attempt, not only when the producer is sent back. The tests it names would fail on the base tree and pass with the change, and the dependents it lists are mostly right. But the reading's root cause does not hold up against the code, and the plan inherits the error. The failure class was reported by introspection, and introspection builds its "stored event" only from the job's title, the outcome reason and verification.json (`event_of_job` and `failure_details` in introspect.rs). Its system prompt says it can read nothing else. It never sees producer invocation details. The verifier never sees the producer report either (D32). The producer's per-criterion check, with status and evidence for every criterion, is also already stored on the passing path in `candidate.producer_report` (candidate.rs:83, records.rs:821). So the change mostly copies data that already exists into a field that neither audience reads. The next failed job would still produce "nothing in the stored event shows the criterion being checked". The request asked to give the information to the failing stage's inputs. That place is `event_of_job` and the introspection event, not `producer_loop`. The planner can fix this by keeping the producer.rs change if wanted, and adding the pre-verdict check (from `candidate.producer_report.criteria_check` and the stored self-check details) to the event's `what`. It also needs a test that builds an event for a job rejected on an unmet criterion and asserts the pre-verdict status of that criterion appears in it. Findings: major: The fix stores data where the stage that reported the failure never looks, so the failure class stays. (Reading root cause; plan Approach and Decision 1; crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs:1473-1508, 984-1060, 1062-1064); major: The claim that a passing self-check leaves no stored record is false: the passing report's per-criterion check is already stored. (Reading root cause; plan Approach ('A check that finds every criterion met ... stores nothing'); crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs:64-83; crates/athena-data/src/records.rs:815-821, 863); major: The tests only show that the producer's own record gained a string. They do not show that the reader of the stored event (introspection) now sees the pre-verdict check. (Demonstrations for criteria 3 and 4); minor: Putting free-text evidence before `; redacted report: ` can break the existing parse of the stored detail. (Plan Decision 3 / Step 4; crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs:1799); minor: briefs.rs is an expected deliverable, but the plan leaves it unchanged. Without a reason in the report, the producer gets sent back for an unchanged planned file. (Expected deliverables vs plan Files (briefs.rs); crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:337, 484); nit: Setting `attempt.detail` on the passing path overwrites any detail the driver set on a successful run. (Plan Step 3)
